question.text: In a radioactive decay chain, the initial nucleus is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msubsup><mi> </mi><mn>90</mn><mn>232</mn></msubsup><mi>Th</mi></math>. At the end, there are <math><mn>6</mn></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>-particles and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>β</mi></math>-particles which are emitted. If the end nucleus is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msubsup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>Z</mi></math> are given by:

solution.text:
As we know that in alpha decay mass number reduced from for and the atomic number reduced by two

and in beta decay the mass number became unchange and atomic number increase from one

Change in Z=6×2-4=8
Change in A=6×4-4=8
